chunks: And it is narrated from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

The Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام ruled concerning a man whose one eye was injured that an ostrich egg should be taken and he should be made to walk with it, and his sound eye should be bound so that he cannot see with it, until the extent of his vision is reached. Then the difference between the limit of the vision of his injured eye and his sound eye should be calculated, and compensation should be paid according to that calculation.

key_terms.بَيْضَةُ نَعَامَةٍ: an ostrich egg used here as part of the procedure for testing visual range
key_terms.عَيْنُهُ الصَّحِيحَةُ: the person’s healthy eye, which is covered during the assessment
key_terms.فَيُؤَدَّى بِحِسَابِ ذَلِكَ: compensation is paid in proportion to the measured loss
key_terms.مُنْتَهَى بَصَرِ: the furthest limit of eyesight or visual range

ai.seo_question: How is compensation assessed in Shia fiqh for partial loss of vision in one eye?
ai.summary: This hadith records a judicial ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام on assessing compensation for partial loss of sight in one eye. It describes a practical method for measuring the injured eye’s visual range against the healthy eye so that payment may be determined proportionally.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5287 - It is narrated from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said:

"The Commander of the Faithful (as) ruled concerning a man who lost one of his eyes that an ostrich egg should be taken, and the man's healthy eye should be covered so he cannot see with it. Then, his vision should be measured to its limit, and the distance between the range of his injured eye and his healthy eye should be calculated. Compensation should be paid accordingly based on that measurement."
